title: Review of c42's CIPS-predator negative on fresh seed 5: replicated; predators from t=0 prevent any prey body, predators introduced at t=3000 dissolve the 4 prey within ~200 t, and the predator enzyme never condenses (max q 0.135)
summary: Three labkit runs of the finding's world on seed 5 (128^2, t=8000): defaults (q0 0.06 from t=0): 0 prey bodies at every sampled time, max q stays at q0 0.06; late introduction (t_intro 3000, q0 0.1, chiq 10, y2 0.1, the g4-type arm): 4 prey bodies at t=800-2800, 0 by t=3200, max q 0.135 at t=3200 then 0.10; prey-only twin (pred_on 0): 4 -> 9 prey bodies by t=8000. The predator eats as a uniform solution and never forms a body, as the finding says. A Cahn-Hilliard prey that survives a distributed loss (c42's own suggestion) does carry a conserved catalysis-condensing consumer: 20261026T1700-c43-cips-consumer.

observations.F: rerun/seed5: 0 prey bodies t=0-8000, max q = 0.06 (bath); rerun_late/seed5/sheet.png: prey present t=700-2800, gone by t=3100-3500 after q is introduced at 3000, max q 0.135 -> 0.10, never a predator body; rerun_preyonly/seed5: prey 4 -> 9

seeds_run.result: pass: no predator condensate in either arm; prey destroyed in both

controls_run.F: rerun_preyonly/seed5 (pred_on 0, matched seed, grid and duration)

not_checked: the other 15 parameter sets of the finding
verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and two of the finding's 17 predator settings. labkit's per-species robust threshold reports one 'predator' track in the late arm, but max q never exceeds 0.135, so it is a bath fluctuation, not a body.
